claim: Activation of TRPV1 channels in sensory neurons results in opening of a cation permeation pathway that triggers the sensation of pain.
source: Activation of TRPV1 channels in sensory neurons results in opening of a cation permeation pathway that triggers the sensation of pain.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about TRPV1 function in pain sensation.

claim: Opening of TRPV1 has been proposed to involve two gates: the ion selectivity filter on the external side of the pore and the S6 helices that line the cytosolic half of the pore.
source: Opening of TRPV1 has been proposed to involve two gates that appear to prevent ion permeation in the absence of activators: the ion selectivity filter on the external side of the pore and the S6 helices that line the cytosolic half of the pore.
evidence: This refers to a hypothesis in the field based on prior work, citing existing proposals.

claim: Cations can permeate the ion selectivity filters of TRPV1-3 channels even when channels are closed.
source: Although our results are consistent with structural evidence that the selectivity filters in these channels are dynamic, they demonstrate that cations can permeate the ion selectivity filters even when channels are closed.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The selectivity filters in TRPV1-3 channels do not function as activation gates.
source: Our results suggest that the selectivity filters in TRPV1-3 channels do not function as activation gates but might contribute to coupling structural rearrangements in the external pore to those in the cytosolic S6 gate.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The selectivity filters in TRPV1-3 channels might contribute to coupling structural rearrangements in the external pore to those in the cytosolic S6 gate.
source: Our results suggest that the selectivity filters in TRPV1-3 channels do not function as activation gates but might contribute to coupling structural rearrangements in the external pore to those in the cytosolic S6 gate.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data regarding the functional role of the selectivity filter.

claim: TRP ion channels are involved in multiple important biological processes in organisms from yeast to mammals.
source: Transient Receptor Potential (TRP) ion channels are involved in multiple important biological processes in organisms from yeast to mammals (Li, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: TRP channels are involved in organelle function and trafficking in single cells.
source: These processes range from organelle function and trafficking in single cells (Zhang et al., 2018b) to the primary detection of sensory stimuli (Mickle et al., 2015) and whole-animal thermoregulation (Wang and Siemens, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: TRP channels are involved in the primary detection of sensory stimuli.
source: These processes range from organelle function and trafficking in single cells (Zhang et al., 2018b) to the primary detection of sensory stimuli (Mickle et al., 2015) and whole-animal thermoregulation (Wang and Siemens, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: TRP channels are involved in whole-animal thermoregulation.
source: These processes range from organelle function and trafficking in single cells (Zhang et al., 2018b) to the primary detection of sensory stimuli (Mickle et al., 2015) and whole-animal thermoregulation (Wang and Siemens, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: TRPV1 is important due to its role as an integrator of pain-producing stimuli and inflammatory mediators in nociceptive sensory neurons.
source: TRPV1 is particularly important due to its role as an integrator of pain-producing stimuli and inflammatory mediators in nociceptive sensory neurons (Moore et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Vertebrates express 27 TRP channel genes, grouped into six subfamilies.
source: Vertebrates express 27 TRP channel genes, grouped into six subfamilies: TRPA – Ankyrin; TRPC – Canonical; TRPM – Melastatin; TRPML – Mucolipin; TRPP – Polycystin; TRPV – Vanilloid.
evidence: This is established knowledge about TRP channel classification.

claim: TRP channels assemble as homo- or hetero-tetramers.
source: TRP channels assemble as homo- or hetero-tetramers with cytosolic domains that differ in size and structure between subfamilies, and a transmembrane domain fold that is very similar between all members of the family.
evidence: This is established knowledge about TRP channel structure.

claim: Each TRP channel subunit contains six transmembrane helices (S1-S6) that fold in a similar way to voltage-gated cation channels.
source: Each subunit contains six transmembrane helices (S1-S6) that fold in a similar way to voltage-gated cation channels (Madej and Ziegler, 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The S1-S4 helices from each TRP channel subunit form modulatory domains that surround the central cation-conducting pathway formed by four sets of S5 and S6 helices.
source: The S1-S4 helices from each subunit form modulatory domains that surround the central cation-conducting pathway formed by four sets of S5 and S6 helices (Figure 1) (Zhang et al., 2018b).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation and reference to Figure 1.

claim: A low concentration of free Ag+ (50 nM) reversibly inhibited whole-cell currents activated by 2-APB and capsaicin in Cys-less TRPV1 channels.
source: We therefore began by testing a TRPV1 construct without native cysteines (Cys-less TRPV1) (Salazar et al., 2008; Salazar et al., 2009) and found that a low concentration of free Ag+ (50 nM) reversibly inhibited whole-cell currents activated by two different TRPV1 ligands: 2-aminoethyldiphenyl borinate (2-APB) and capsaicin (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study, supported by data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The apparent affinity for Ag+ decreased steeply with depolarization to positive membrane potentials in Cys-less TRPV1 channels.
source: The apparent affinity for Ag+ decreased steeply with depolarization to positive membrane potentials (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study, supported by data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The slope of the voltage-dependence relationship (Zδ=−0.89) is equivalent to the transfer of a monovalent cation across 89% of the transmembrane electric field.
source: The slope of this relationship (Zδ=−0.89) is equivalent to the transfer of a monovalent cation across 89% of the transmembrane electric field (Woodhull, 1973), strongly suggesting that Ag+ ions block TRPV1 channels by binding within the pore, instead of allosterically inhibiting channel activation from outside the cation conduction pathway.
evidence: This is an interpretation of experimental data using a cited theoretical framework.

claim: Ag+ ions block TRPV1 channels by binding within the pore, instead of allosterically inhibiting channel activation from outside the cation conduction pathway.
source: The slope of this relationship (Zδ=−0.89) is equivalent to the transfer of a monovalent cation across 89% of the transmembrane electric field (Woodhull, 1973), strongly suggesting that Ag+ ions block TRPV1 channels by binding within the pore, instead of allosterically inhibiting channel activation from outside the cation conduction pathway.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data and theoretical considerations.

claim: The apparent affinity of TRPV1 for Ag+ ions increased > 10 fold when measured at a lower capsaicin concentration (50 nM) where the open probability was ~10 fold lower.
source: In contrast, we observed a > 10 fold increase in the apparent affinity for Ag+ (Figure 2D,F and G) when we measured the concentration-response relation for Ag+ using a lower capsaicin concentration (50 nM) where the open probability of the channels was ~10 fold lower, as measured from conductance-voltage relations at the two capsaicin concentrations (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study, supported by data shown in Figures 2D, 2F, 2G, and 2H.

claim: The prominent state-dependence of the apparent affinity of TRPV1 for Ag+ ions strongly suggests that the filter undergoes a conformational change when channels activate.
source: The prominent state-dependence of the apparent affinity of TRPV1 for Ag+ ions, which are likely to interact with the filter based on the high affinity and voltage-dependence associated with block, strongly suggest that the filter undergoes a conformational change when channels activate.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations of state-dependent Ag+ affinity.

claim: Ag+ binds more tightly to closed than to open TRPV1 channels at equilibrium.
source: Although our findings indicate that Ag+ ions bind more tightly to closed than to open channels at equilibrium, they provide no information about how gating influences Ag+ accessibility.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings regarding Ag+ binding affinity.

claim: Ag+ reversibly inhibited Cys-less Δturret TRPV1 channels.
source: As we observed previously with Cys-less TRPV1 channels, Ag+ reversibly inhibited Cys-less Δturret channels (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study, supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Repeated stimulation of Cys-less Δturret channels with 2-APB resulted in a slow, progressive decrease in current (rundown).
source: repeated stimulation of Cys-less Δturret channels with 2-APB resulted in a slow, progressive decrease in current (i.e. rundown), but the rundown measured from six initial rounds of stimulation with 2-APB without Ag+ appeared unaffected by subsequent exposures to Ag+ (Figure 3C, gray symbols), indicating that Ag+ has no irreversible effects on our Cys-less Δturret background construct.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study, supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Ag+ has no irreversible effects on Cys-less Δturret TRPV1 background construct.
source: repeated stimulation of Cys-less Δturret channels with 2-APB resulted in a slow, progressive decrease in current (i.e. rundown), but the rundown measured from six initial rounds of stimulation with 2-APB without Ag+ appeared unaffected by subsequent exposures to Ag+ (Figure 3C, gray symbols), indicating that Ag+ has no irreversible effects on our Cys-less Δturret background construct.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observation that rundown was unaffected by Ag+ exposure.

claim: 2-APB does not directly interact with Ag+ ions.
source: Importantly, we verified that 2-APB does not directly interact with Ag+ ions by showing that the presence of 2-APB does not alter the rate of modification by Ag+ of a pore-facing cysteine in a P2X2 receptor construct (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B C) that was characterized previously (Li et al., 2008).
evidence: This is an experimental verification using a control experiment with P2X2 receptors, supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B C.

claim: When TRPV1 channels are open, external Ag+ can traverse the filter and bind tightly to I679C, permanently obstructing Na+ currents.
source: The irreversible inhibition by Ag+ indicates that, when channels are open, external Ag+ can traverse the filter and bind tightly to I679C, permanently obstructing Na+ currents.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observation of irreversible inhibition by Ag+.

claim: The fold-change in Po resulting from channel activation by 2-APB is well above 100-fold in Cys-less Δturret + I679C TRPV1 channels.
source: By measuring the ratio of the current magnitude with and without agonist we estimated that the fold-change in Po resulting from channel activation by 2-APB is well above 100-fold (Figure 3K, light blue).
evidence: This is an experimental estimate based on current measurements, supported by data shown in Figure 3K.

claim: The time courses and corresponding rates of cysteine modification by Ag+ were very similar when Ag+ was applied with or without 2-APB or capsaicin (<3 fold difference) in Cys-less Δturret + I679C TRPV1 channels.
source: We performed these experiments (Figure 3B) and found that the time courses (Figure 3C–D) and corresponding rates of cysteine modification (Figure 3J) were very similar when Ag+ was applied with or without 2-APB or capsaicin (<3 fold difference, Figure 3K, light blue).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study, supported by data shown in Figures 3B, 3C-D, 3J, and 3K.

claim: External Ag+ has similar accessibility to I679C in both the open and closed states of TRPV1 channels.
source: These results reveal that external Ag+ has similar accessibility to I679C in both the open and closed states, strongly suggesting that the filter is not an activation gate.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing similar modification rates in open and closed states.

claim: The rate of irreversible inhibition by Ag+ in the open state measured for I679C (3.27 ± 0.57×10^7 M−1s−1) is near the limit of diffusion.
source: Arguing against this possibility, the rate of irreversible inhibition by Ag+ in the open state that we measured (3.27 ± 0.57×107 M−1s−1) is near the limit of diffusion, and falls within the same range as open-state modification rates by Ag+ measured in other cation channels (del Camino and Yellen, 2001; Flynn and Zagotta, 2001; Contreras et al., 2008; Li et al., 2008).
evidence: This is an experimental measurement compared to known diffusion limits and literature values.

claim: The rates of modification in the open state became measurably slower at lower Ag+ concentrations in Cys-less Δturret + I679C TRPV1 channels.
source: The rates of modification in the open state became measurably slower at the lower Ag+-concentrations (Figure 3E, bottom panel, yellow), indicating that accessibility does indeed limit the rates of modification that we measure in our experiments.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study, supported by data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The rates of modification in the closed state showed the same concentration-dependent trend as in the open state in Cys-less Δturret + I679C TRPV1 channels.
source: More importantly, the rates of modification in the closed state showed the same trend (Figure 3E, bottom panel, gray), resulting in a state-dependent ratio of open to closed-state modification that remained virtually constant over the entire range of Ag+-concentrations (Figure 3E, top panel).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study, supported by data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The lack of state-dependence in modification rates demonstrates that the filter of TRPV1 does not function as an activation gate.
source: These results demonstrate that our rates of modification closely report on Ag+-accessibility, and that the lack of state-dependence that we observe demonstrates that the filter of TRPV1 does not function as an activation gate.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing similar modification rates in open and closed states across different Ag+ concentrations.

claim: Negative membrane potentials have a strong positive influence on the rate of I679C modification by Ag+ for both open and closed states of TRPV1 channels.
source: The data reveal that negative membrane potentials have a strong positive influence on the rate of I679C modification by Ag+ for both open and closed states (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study, supported by data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Ag+ reaches I679C in both the open and closed states of TRPV1 channels by permeating through a large fraction of the transmembrane electric field.
source: This provides further evidence that Ag+ reaches I679C in both the open and closed states of the channel by permeating through a large fraction of the transmembrane electric field (Sobolevsky et al., 2005; Contreras et al., 2010).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the voltage-dependence of modification rates, supported by citations to theoretical frameworks.

claim: The rate of modification by Ag+ was <10 fold slower in the absence than in the presence of 2-APB for C157A + I679C TRPV1 channels.
source: To verify that our data aren't specific to the background construct or the location of the inserted cysteine, we performed experiments using either a full-length construct with all but one native cysteine known to influence gating upon reaction with intracellular cysteine-modifying agents (C157A + I679C) (Salazar et al., 2008; Salazar et al., 2009) (Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplement 1G–H) or a Cys-less Δturret construct with a cysteine introduced immediately below the filter at I642 (Figure 1, Figure 3H, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1I–K). In both cases we found that the rate of modification by Ag+ was <10 fold slower in the absence than in the presence of 2-APB, whereas Po changed by >100 fold upon stimulation with 2-APB (Figure 3J and K).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study, supported by data shown in Figures 3G, 3H, 3J, 3K, and figure supplements.

claim: The rate of modification by Ag+ was <10 fold slower in the absence than in the presence of 2-APB for Cys-less Δturret + I642C TRPV1 channels.
source: To verify that our data aren't specific to the background construct or the location of the inserted cysteine, we performed experiments using either a full-length construct with all but one native cysteine known to influence gating upon reaction with intracellular cysteine-modifying agents (C157A + I679C) (Salazar et al., 2008; Salazar et al., 2009) (Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplement 1G–H) or a Cys-less Δturret construct with a cysteine introduced immediately below the filter at I642 (Figure 1, Figure 3H, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1I–K). In both cases we found that the rate of modification by Ag+ was <10 fold slower in the absence than in the presence of 2-APB, whereas Po changed by >100 fold upon stimulation with 2-APB (Figure 3J and K).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study, supported by data shown in Figures 3H, 3J, 3K, and figure supplements.

claim: The rates of modification for I642C were not influenced by voltage in TRPV1 channels.
source: However, in contrast with our data using I679C, the rates of modification for I642C were not influenced by voltage (Figure 3I).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study, supported by data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: There was no consistent correlation between the rates of modification and the estimated change in Po by 2-APB in closed state Ag+-accessibility experiments for TRPV1 channels.
source: Finally, we found no consistent correlation between the rates of modification and the estimated change in Po by 2-APB in any of our closed state Ag+-accessibility experiments (Figure 3—figure supplement 5), lending further support to the conclusion that the selectivity filter of the TRPV1 channel is not an activation gate.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study, supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 5.

claim: Multiple stimuli influence gating of TRPV1 by targeting the external pore, including cations and toxins from venomous animals.
source: Multiple stimuli, including cations (Tominaga et al., 1998; Cao et al., 2014; Jara-Oseguera et al., 2016) and toxins from venomous animals (Bohlen et al., 2010; Cao et al., 2013; Yang et al., 2015b), influence gating of TRPV1 by targeting the external pore.
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: No modulators that target the external pore are known for TRPV2 and TRPV3 channels.
source: In contrast, no such modulators are known for its two close homologues, TRPV2 and TRPV3 (Smith et al., 2002; Ryu et al., 2007; Gao et al., 2016a).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The selectivity filter of TRPV2 adopts non-conducting conformations in some of the available structures.
source: As discussed above for TRPV1, the selectivity filter of TRPV2 adopts non-conducting conformations in some of the available structures (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) (Zubcevic et al., 2016; Zubcevic et al., 2018b; Dosey et al., 2019; Zubcevic et al., 2019b) and the filter has been suggested to function as a gate.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to structural studies and reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The selectivity filter of TRPV3 is more solvent accessible in the absence of activators compared to TRPV1 and TRPV2.
source: In contrast, the selectivity filter of TRPV3 is more solvent accessible in the absence of activators compared to TRPV1 and TRPV2 and has not been observed to undergo substantial structural changes in the presence of activators (Singh et al., 2018; Zubcevic et al., 2018a; Zubcevic et al., 2019a).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to structural studies.

claim: TRPV2-QM was reversibly blocked by Ag+ in a similar way to Cys-less TRPV1.
source: Experiments using 4 mM 2-APB as an activator confirmed that TRPV2-QM was reversibly blocked by Ag+ in a similar way to Cys-less TRPV1 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), indicating that it constitutes a good background for our experiments because Ag+ has no irreversible effects on this construct even after repeated exposures to Ag+ (Figure 4B and E, gray triangles).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study, supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and Figure 4B and E.

claim: TRPV2-QM + I642C channels exhibited a pronounced rundown upon repeated stimulation with 2-APB in the absence of Ag+.
source: To our surprise, we found that TRPV2-QM + I642C channels exhibited a pronounced rundown upon repeated stimulation with 2-APB in the absence of Ag+ (Figure 4A and B, empty circles).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study, supported by data shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: Irreversible cysteine modification by Ag+ was more rapid than rundown in rTRPV2-QM + I642C channels.
source: We proceeded to perform accessibility experiments for rTRPV2-QM + I642C channels in which we applied Ag+ either during or after 2-APB application (Figure 4C). In both cases, we found that irreversible cysteine modification by Ag+ was more rapid than rundown, indicating that cysteine residues at I642C efficiently coordinate Ag+ (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study, supported by data shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: The rundown-corrected time courses for irreversible cysteine modification by Ag+ in the open or closed states of rTRPV2-QM + I642C channels were less than 3-fold different.
source: Importantly, the rundown-corrected time courses for irreversible cysteine modification by Ag+ in the open or closed states (Figure 4E), and their associated rates of cysteine modification (Figure 4F), were less than 3-fold different (although this difference was indeed statistically significant).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study, supported by data shown in Figure 4E and F.

claim: 2-APB increased Po by a factor >100 in rTRPV2-QM + I642C channels.
source: On the other hand, 2-APB increased Po by a factor >100 in these channels (Figure 4G), indicating that the filter is not an activation gate in TRPV2 channels.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study, supported by data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The filter is not an activation gate in TRPV2 channels.
source: On the other hand, 2-APB increased Po by a factor >100 in these channels (Figure 4G), indicating that the filter is not an activation gate in TRPV2 channels.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing similar modification rates despite large changes in Po.

claim: Ag+ is not an effective pore-blocker of WT mTRPV3 channels.
source: To investigate Ag+ accessibility in the TRPV3 channel, we initially tested whether Ag+ has any effect on WT mTRPV3 channels and surprisingly discovered that unlike TRPV1 and TRPV2, Ag+ is not an effective pore-blocker (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study, supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The time-courses of modification when Ag+ was applied in the presence and absence of 2-APB and the associated rates were very similar for mTRPV3 + I674C channels.
source: As with TRPV1 and TRPV2, the time-courses of modification when Ag+ was applied in the presence and absence of 2-APB (Figure 5A–B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C) and the associated rates (Figure 5D) were very similar.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study, supported by data shown in Figures 5A-B, 5D, and figure supplement.

claim: mTRPV3 + I674C channels contribute substantially to the baseline currents.
source: When we plotted the time courses of Ag+-mediated decay in baseline as a function of exposure time to Ag+ (Figure 5B, insert), the rates were identical to the decay measured from the steady-state currents in 2-APB. This indicates that mTRPV3 + I674C channels contribute substantially to the baseline currents.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observation that baseline and 2-APB-activated currents showed identical decay rates.

claim: The increased baseline in mTRPV3 + I674C channels does not arise from incomplete deactivation after 2-APB removal, but rather from a higher baseline Po.
source: Increasing the time interval between 2-APB removal and Ag+ application did not alter the rates of modification (Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C), indicating that the increased baseline does not arise from incomplete deactivation after 2-APB removal, but rather from a higher baseline Po.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observation that modification rates were independent of washout time.

claim: The state-dependence of the rates of modification was smaller than the estimated change in Po by 2-APB for mTRPV3 + I674C channels.
source: Regardless, the state-dependence of the rates of modification was smaller than the estimated change in Po by 2-APB (Figure 5E, dark blue), indicating that the filter of mTRPV3 is not an activation gate.
evidence: This is an experimental observation and conclusion from the study, supported by data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The filter of mTRPV3 is not an activation gate.
source: Regardless, the state-dependence of the rates of modification was smaller than the estimated change in Po by 2-APB (Figure 5E, dark blue), indicating that the filter of mTRPV3 is not an activation gate.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing that state-dependence of modification is smaller than the change in Po.

claim: Modification of mTRPV3 + I674C by Ag+ was detectably faster in the absence of external Na+ ions.
source: We thus performed experiments with TRPV3 + I674C channels in which Ag+ ions were applied in the absence of both 2-APB and external Na+ (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D). We found that modification was detectably faster in the absence of external Na+ ions, but not as fast as when 2-APB was also included (Figure 5B and D).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study, supported by data shown in Figure 5B, D, and figure supplement.

claim: Interactions between Ag+ and Na+ ions in the pore contribute to the observed state-dependence of Ag+ accessibility in mTRPV3 channels.
source: This suggests that interactions between Ag+ and Na+ ions in the pore contribute to the observed state-dependence of Ag+ accessibility.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observation that modification was faster in the absence of external Na+.

claim: The time courses of modification and the associated rates for mTRPV3 + I637C channels showed marginal state-dependence.
source: Finally, we performed accessibility experiments with mTRPV3 channels with a cysteine introduced immediately below the filter at a site that aligns with position I642 in TRPV1 (I637C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B). Unlike the I674C mutation, mTRPV3 + I637C channels did not exhibit baseline channel activity in the absence of 2-APB (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E). Nevertheless, the time courses of modification (Figure 5C) and the associated rates again showed marginal state-dependence (Figure 5D and E, purple).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study, supported by data shown in Figures 5C, 5D, 5E, and figure supplement.

claim: The absence of a role for the selectivity filter in TRPV1 gating can be extended to TRPV2 and TRPV3 channels.
source: Together, our results indicate that the absence of a role for the selectivity filter in TRPV1 gating can be extended to TRPV2 and TRPV3 channels.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data across all three channel types.

claim: The pore of TRPV1 channels has been suggested to 'dilate' upon prolonged activation, resulting in increased permeability to large organic cations.
source: The pore of TRPV1 channels has been suggested to 'dilate' upon prolonged activation, resulting in increased permeability to large organic cations (Chung et al., 2008; Munns et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Structural changes in the selectivity filter are thought to be necessary for permeation of large organic cations through TRPV2 channels.
source: Structural changes in the selectivity filter are also thought to be necessary for permeation of large organic cations through TRPV2 channels (Zubcevic et al., 2018b; Zubcevic et al., 2019b).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Prominent rundown-corrected MTSEA-dependent current inhibition was observed in both closed- and open-state experiments with Cys-less Δturret + I679C TRPV1 channels.
source: Prominent rundown-corrected MTSEA-dependent current inhibition was observed in both closed- (Figure 6B, gray symbols) and open-state experiments (Figure 6B, yellow symbols), indicating that MTSEA can gain access to I679C in both states of the channel.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study, supported by data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: MTSEA can gain access to I679C in both open and closed states of TRPV1 channels.
source: Prominent rundown-corrected MTSEA-dependent current inhibition was observed in both closed- (Figure 6B, gray symbols) and open-state experiments (Figure 6B, yellow symbols), indicating that MTSEA can gain access to I679C in both states of the channel.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observation of MTSEA-dependent inhibition in both states.

claim: The time courses of modification by MTSEA and the associated time constants were ~20 fold faster in the presence of capsaicin than in its absence for Cys-less Δturret + I679C TRPV1 channels.
source: The time courses of modification by MTSEA (Figure 6B; gray and yellow) and the associated time constants (Figure 6H) were ~20 fold faster in the presence of capsaicin than in its absence.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study, supported by data shown in Figure 6B and H.

claim: The change in Po caused by capsaicin (>50 fold) was larger than the decrease in the time constant of modification by MTSEA.
source: Yet, the change in Po caused by the agonist (>50 fold) was still larger than the decrease in the time constant of modification (τ) (Figure 6I, turquoise and white bars), suggesting that the filter does not fully gate access to MTSEA.
evidence: This is an experimental observation and inference from the study, supported by data shown in Figure 6I.

claim: The filter does not fully gate access to MTSEA in TRPV1 channels.
source: Yet, the change in Po caused by the agonist (>50 fold) was still larger than the decrease in the time constant of modification (τ) (Figure 6I, turquoise and white bars), suggesting that the filter does not fully gate access to MTSEA.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the comparison of Po change and modification time constant change.

claim: The trend in MTSEA modification time constants correlates with the concentration of MTSEA+ and not MTSEA0.
source: The trend in the experiments (Figure 6B; τpink > τblue > τpurple > τgray) correlates with the concentration of MTSEA+ and not MTSEA0 (Figure 6F, solid lines) and can also be well described by our model using concentrations for MTSEA that closely match those of MTSEA+ in each of the experiments (Figure 6F, dotted curve).
evidence: This is an experimental observation and modeling result from the study, supported by data shown in Figure 6B and F.

claim: MTSEA+ can gain access through the filter when TRPV1 channels are closed.
source: We thus conclude that MTSEA+ can gain access through the filter when the channel is closed.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing that MTSEA+ concentration correlates with modification rates.

claim: Slow accessibility of MTSET was found in the open state and undetectable accessibility in the closed state of Cys-less Δturret + I679C TRPV1 channels.
source: Finally, in accessibility experiments with the larger and positively charged MTSET (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E), we found slow accessibility in the open state and undetectable accessibility in the closed state that was indistinguishable from rundown (Figure 6G and Figure 6—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study, supported by data shown in Figure 6G and figure supplement.

claim: The ratio between the time constants of cysteine modification by MTSET in the closed vs the open state was noticeably larger than the fold-change in Po caused by capsaicin.
source: In addition, the ratio between the time constants of cysteine modification by MTSET in the closed vs the open state (Figure 6H) was for the first time noticeably larger than the fold-change in Po caused by capsaicin (Figure 6I, light blue and white bars).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study, supported by data shown in Figure 6H and I.

claim: The state dependence of accessibility across the selectivity filter to I679C increases with the size of permeant cations.
source: This indicates that the state dependence of accessibility across the selectivity filter to I679C increases with the size of permeant cations.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations with Ag+, MTSEA, and MTSET.

claim: TRPV1, TRPV2 and TRPV3 channels are gated by the S6 helices on the cytosolic side of the pore.
source: Our findings necessarily imply that TRPV1, TRPV2 and TRPV3 channels are gated by the S6 helices on the cytosolic side of the pore.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings that the selectivity filter does not function as an activation gate.

claim: The S6 helices function as the activation gate in all members of the TRP channel family.
source: This strongly suggests that the S6 helices function as the activation gate in all members of the TRP channel family.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from structural data across TRP channel subfamilies showing conserved cytosolic constrictions.

claim: Y671 in TRPV1 is the inner-most site in S6 that exhibits state-dependent modification by cytosolic Ag+.
source: This latter study scanned the S6 helix of TRPV1 for accessibility to cytosolic Ag+ and identified Y671 as the inner-most site in S6 that exhibits state-dependent modification (Salazar et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Molecular dynamics simulations reveal the potential presence of an aqueous pathway between the S1-S4 and pore domain in TRPV1 through which Ag+ ions could reach S6 cysteines located beyond the I679 gate.
source: Molecular dynamics simulations reveal the potential presence of an aqueous pathway between the S1-S4 and pore domain in TRPV1 through which Ag+ ions could reach S6 cysteines located beyond the I679 gate (Kasimova et al., 2018), providing a possible explanation for this discrepancy.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a molecular dynamics study.

claim: The agonist-induced structural differences in the filters of TRPV1 and TRPV2 channel structures suggest that the external pore and the selectivity filter undergo activation-dependent conformational changes.
source: The agonist-induced structural differences in the filters of TRPV1 (Cao et al., 2013; Gao et al., 2016b) and TRPV2 (Zubcevic et al., 2018b; Zubcevic et al., 2019b) channel structures suggest that the external pore and the selectivity filter undergo activation-dependent conformational changes, in which 'wider' filter openings correspond to activated states.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from structural comparisons in the cited literature.

claim: Mutations proposed to disrupt agonist-induced conformational changes in the filter of TRPV2 impair permeation of large organic cations without noticeably affecting Na+ currents.
source: Moreover, mutations proposed to disrupt agonist-induced conformational changes in the filter of TRPV2 impair permeation of large organic cations without noticeably affecting Na+ currents (Zubcevic et al., 2018b).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The modulation of the single-channel current amplitude of the TRPV1 channel by extracellular protons and other cations provides support that the selectivity filter is a dynamic structure.
source: The modulation of the single-channel current amplitude of the TRPV1 channel by extracellular protons (Liu et al., 2009; Lee and Zheng, 2015) and other cations (Cao et al., 2014), and the large state-dependence for block by Ag+ that we detected in this study provide further support that the selectivity filter is a dynamic structure that can adopt multiple ligand-dependent conformations.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from cited literature and the experimental data in this study.

claim: The external pore and selectivity filter of TRPV1 are in a dynamic equilibrium between distinct conformations, and channel activation favors those that enable more rapid permeation of large cations.
source: We therefore propose that the external pore and selectivity filter of TRPV1 are in a dynamic equilibrium between distinct conformations, and that channel activation favors those that enable more rapid permeation of large cations.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental data showing increased state-dependence for larger cations.

claim: The data don't support the idea that permeability to large cations continues to increase once activation reaches equilibrium in TRPV1 channels.
source: Contrary to the 'pore-dilation' hypothesis (Chung et al., 2008; Munns et al., 2015), however, our data don't support the idea that permeability to large cations continues to increase once activation reaches equilibrium (within a few seconds).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations and comparison to prior hypotheses.

claim: Different agonists result in distinct single-channel current amplitudes for TRPV1, but the values remain stable during long recording periods.
source: Moreover, even though different agonists result in distinct single-channel current amplitudes for TRPV1, the values remain stable during long recording periods (Hui et al., 2003; Canul-Sánchez et al., 2018; Geron et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The permeability of Ca2+ relative to Na+ in TRPV1 has been shown to remain stable during long agonist applications.
source: Also, the permeability of Ca2+ relative to Na+ in TRPV1 has been shown to remain stable during long agonist applications (Samways et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Observations originally interpreted as dilation of the pore in P2X receptors were subsequently shown to result from accumulation or depletion of ions inside the cell.
source: P2X receptors are also permeable to organic cations, and observations originally interpreted as dilation of the pore were subsequently shown to result from accumulation or depletion of ions inside the cell (Li et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The selectivity filter functions as an actuator after adopting its active conformation to stabilize the cytosolic gate in an open conformation.
source: To reconcile our findings with the structural and experimental observations of activation-dependent conformational changes in the selectivity filter and external pore region we propose that the selectivity filter functions as an actuator after adopting its active conformation to stabilize the cytosolic gate in an open conformation (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a proposed model to explain the experimental findings and structural observations.

claim: The selectivity filter functioning as an actuator could constitute the mechanism by which multiple stimuli that target the external pore of TRPV1 promote opening of the cytosolic gate.
source: This could constitute the mechanism by which the multiple stimuli that target the external pore of the TRPV1 channel promote opening of the cytosolic gate.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the proposed model.

claim: Diverse stimuli that target the external pore of TRPV1 include H+, other cations, pain-producing toxins from poisonous animals, and possibly heat.
source: These diverse stimuli include H+ (Jordt et al., 2000) and other cations (Cao et al., 2014; Jara-Oseguera et al., 2016), pain-producing toxins from poisonous animals (Bohlen et al., 2010; Cao et al., 2013; Yang et al., 2015b; Bae et al., 2016; Gao et al., 2016b), and possibly heat (Grandl et al., 2010; Yang et al., 2015b; Jara-Oseguera et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2018a).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: The mutual coupling between the cytosolic gate and the external pore and filter, and the principle of microscopic reversibility, would ensure that agonists like capsaicin and resiniferatoxin result in the stabilization of the selectivity filter region in its active conformation.
source: Importantly, the mutual coupling between the cytosolic gate and the external pore and filter, and the principle of microscopic reversibility, would ensure that agonists like capsaicin and resiniferatoxin, which appear to induce opening of the cytosolic gate in TRPV1, TRPV2 and TRPV3 channels by acting on the S4-S5 linker helix (Cao et al., 2013; Yang et al., 2015a; Gao et al., 2016b; Zubcevic et al., 2018b; Zhang et al., 2019; Zubcevic et al., 2019b), also result in the stabilization of the selectivity filter region in its active conformation.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the proposed coupling mechanism and thermodynamic principles, supported by citations.

claim: The molecular mechanism of coupling between the cytosolic gate and the selectivity filter is not known, but in TRPV1 it has been suggested to involve interactions between T641 in the pore helix and Y671 in the S6 helix.
source: The molecular mechanism of this coupling is not known, but in TRPV1 it has been suggested to involve interactions between T641 in the pore helix and Y671 in the S6 helix (Steinberg et al., 2017; Kasimova et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: A similar coupling function has been suggested for the equivalent residues in TRPV2.
source: A similar function has been suggested for the equivalent residues in TRPV2 (Zubcevic et al., 2018b; Zubcevic et al., 2019b).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The external pore of TRPV1 has been implicated in temperature-sensing.
source: However, the external pore of TRPV1 has been implicated in temperature-sensing (Grandl et al., 2008; Bae et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2018a), thus structural rearrangements in the selectivity filter region of TRPV2 and TRPV3 may allow this region to function as an actuator for heat activation.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Structural rearrangements in the selectivity filter region of TRPV2 and TRPV3 may allow this region to function as an actuator for heat activation.
source: However, the external pore of TRPV1 has been implicated in temperature-sensing (Grandl et al., 2008; Bae et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2018a), thus structural rearrangements in the selectivity filter region of TRPV2 and TRPV3 may allow this region to function as an actuator for heat activation.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the proposed model and prior literature.
